conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (CONTRIBUTING.md line 25, e.g. 'feat(lang): ...', 'feat(core): add Swift language support ... (#1742)'). Commits must be GPG-signed (git commit -S) and carry 'Signed-off-by:' (DCO); recent commits in git log show the Signed-off-by trailer.
conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/*.rs file (queries_compile, element match, inheritance happy and empty, defuse write, empty file). Registry tests live in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs. Integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/*.rs and use common::call_tool_raw plus tempfile::NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in.
conventions.linting: cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; workspace lints in Cargo.toml: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used = deny; must_use_candidate, redundant_clone, needless_pass_by_value, large_enum_variant = warn; unreachable_pub = warn. REUSE compliance requires an SPDX header on every new file.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec, never Result. Node text uses bounds-checked get_node_text (languages/mod.rs) or an end_byte <= source.len() guard. Query compile errors surface as ParserError::QueryError (parser.rs build_compiled_queries); tests call Query::new(...).expect('... must be valid').

patterns: Registry arm per language in languages/mod.rs get_language_info(): name, language, element_query, call_query, reference_query, import_query, impl_query, impl_trait_query, defuse_query, extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance. Every field is spelled out; there is no Default.

Parallel get_ts_language() match arm returning the grammar LanguageFn .into(); lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP maps extension to language name; supported_languages() must list the name or QUERY_CACHE will not contain it.

Query constants are pub const X: &str = r"..." raw strings, one per capability (ELEMENT, CALL, REFERENCE, IMPORT, DEFUSE). Fortran sets defuse_query: None and markdown/yaml set most fields None: optional capabilities may be omitted.

Capture-name contract (parser_elements.rs): 'function' + 'func_name'|'method_name' for functions and methods; 'class' + 'class_name'|'type_name' for types; 'call' for call sites; 'import_path' for imports; 'type_ref' for references; 'write.*', 'read.*', 'writeread.*' prefixes for def-use. Interface/trait/enum capture names are unused by parser_elements; the name is recovered via child_by_field_name('name').

Java extract_inheritance uses child_by_field_name('superclass') and ('interfaces') and prefixes results 'extends X' / 'implements X'. Swift walks children by kind and prefixes 'extends' for the first and 'conforms' for the rest. PHP has no such fields, so the Swift child-walk style is the correct template.

Fallback import handling (parser_elements.rs ~146-160): any import node kind without a dedicated branch stores its full trimmed text as the module. java's import_declaration and PHP's namespace_use_declaration both rely on this.
Test helper pattern: parse_<lang>(src) with Parser::set_language, then find a node by kind via an explicit stack traversal; or run QueryCursor with StreamingIterator and map capture names.

constraints: supported_languages() in lang.rs builds QUERY_CACHE (parser.rs ~191). get_compiled_queries() (parser.rs ~221) returns UnsupportedLanguage for any name not in that list, and extract_with_depth / extract / extract_module_info / extract_def_use_for_file all call it (parser.rs ~319, 388, 485, 559). So 'php' must be added to supported_languages(), or analyze_file on .php fails.

Latent gap found: 'css' and 'yaml' are in EXTENSION_MAP and get_language_info but NOT in supported_languages() (lang.rs 81-98). By the same logic their extraction paths should fail. Not verified by running tests (read-only). Flag for the maintainers; do not copy this omission for PHP.
The issue requires LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) because .php files commonly mix HTML text with <?php ... ?> tags; the php_only grammar does not parse HTML text.

Scope: five query constants (ELEMENT, CALL, REFERENCE, IMPORT, DEFUSE) plus extract_inheritance; no tool handler or schema changes; .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5 excluded; trait use resolution, properties, constants, attributes and namespace aliasing excluded.
Do not implement extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type for PHP (issue Not in Scope; no consumer since #1807).

Dependency freshness (AGENTS.md): new Cargo.lock entries must be 7+ days old. tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 is tagged 2026-11-19 on GitHub (9 days before this run); the crates.io publish timestamp was not verified (gh and Context7 only).

DEFUSE_QUERY is Option<&str>. Omitting it (as fortran does) silently yields no def-use sites. The issue lists DEFUSE among the five required constants and its acceptance criteria require the handler to 'list ... calls' and inheritance; a def-use query is therefore required by scope.
Clippy promotes must_use_candidate, redundant_clone, needless_pass_by_value and large_enum_variant to warn; new public fns should carry #[must_use] like java.rs does.

approaches.name: A: Mirror java.rs/swift.rs (recommended)
approaches.description: Create languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes, reads), and extract_inheritance using a Swift-style child walk over base_clause and class_interface_clause. Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP. Wire 'php' in lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages(), in languages/mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info arm, get_ts_language arm, registry test row). Add tree-sitter-php to root and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; update README (list and count 18 to 19); add an integration test file.
pros: Matches every acceptance criterion and the five-constant scope in the issue
Same shape as java.rs and swift.rs, so reviewers know the layout
Uses the grammar's named fields (name, body) where they exist and the child walk where the grammar uses anonymous keywords
Captures follow the existing parser_elements contract, so no consumer changes are needed
cons: No local_variable_declaration in PHP: the first assignment stands in as the local declaration, which needs a documented decision
DEFUSE sigil choice: capturing the variable_name node keeps the '$' in the symbol text; callers must pass '$name' (verify with the def-use caller)
Needs the supported_languages() addition, which css/yaml missed

approaches.name: B: Minimal handler (ELEMENT, CALL, IMPORT, inheritance; DEFUSE and REFERENCE None)
approaches.description: Same wiring as A but DEFUSE_QUERY and REFERENCE_QUERY are None, as fortran does for DEFUSE. Only element, call and import queries plus extract_inheritance are written.
pros: Smallest query surface and fewest grammar-specific decisions
Less risk of sigil and scoping mistakes in def-use
cons: Violates the issue's five-query-constant scope and the Acceptance Criteria requirement for a DEFUSE constant
PHP would get no def-use sites, so downstream def-use tools return nothing for PHP

approaches.name: C: Derive ELEMENT/CALL/IMPORT from the grammar's upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Reuse the TAGS_QUERY exported by tree-sitter-php (queries/tags.scm) as the source for ELEMENT_QUERY, remapping its capture names (name, definition.*, reference.*) onto aptu's capture contract (function, func_name, class, class_name, call).
cons: Capture names differ from aptu's contract, so a remapping layer or a rewritten query is needed anyway
tags.scm was not inspected in this scout; coverage and captures are unverified
Harder to review against the issue's explicit element list

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies the issue's five-query scope and acceptance criteria while matching the java.rs and swift.rs template. Use LANGUAGE_PHP. For inheritance, walk the children of class_declaration by kind (base_clause, class_interface_clause), not by field, because the grammar defines no fields for those clauses. Add 'php' to supported_languages() (required, not optional). Record the css/yaml gap as a separate follow-up.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source: php/src/grammar.json at tag v0.25.2 (fetched via gh api; php/grammar.js is a 102-byte stub calling define-grammar('php')). Rules: class_declaration = PREC_RIGHT(seq(optional attributes, repeat _modifier, 'class' token, FIELD name = name, optional base_clause, optional class_interface_clause, FIELD body = declaration_list)). base_clause = seq(ALIAS(PATTERN /extends/i, 'extends' unnamed), seq(_name, repeat(seq(',', _name)))). class_interface_clause = seq(ALIAS(PATTERN /implements/i, 'implements' unnamed), seq(_name, repeat(seq(',', _name)))). _name = choice(name, qualified_name, relative_name). node-types.json: class_declaration has fields name (name) and body (declaration_list), and children base_clause and class_interface_clause with no field names; base_clause and class_interface_clause list name, qualified_name, relative_name as named children; 'extends' and 'implements' are unnamed (named: false). Walk, in Rust: for i in 0..node.child_count(), take child(i). If child.kind() == 'base_clause', iterate named_child(j); for each named child whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name, push format!('extends {text}'). If child.kind() == 'class_interface_clause', do the same and push format!('implements {text}'). Skip the class_declaration name field (kind name) by only descending into the two clause kinds. Expected: class Foo extends Bar implements A, B yields ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; class Plain {} yields []. Do not copy java.rs's child_by_field_name('superclass') walk: PHP defines no such field.
